name: Kreativ Broken Image Finder
description: Catch missing images early and keep content quality high across your site.
cardUse: Catch missing images across posts and pages before users see them.
metaDescription: Detect missing image references across posts and pages before they impact trust and UX.

detailItems.title: A manually started content scan
detailItems.body: Checks image source URLs in published content and featured images using HTTP HEAD requests. It does not inspect every CSS background, responsive image variant, or external page.

detailItems.title: An actionable report
detailItems.body: See affected content, response codes, and missing featured-image entries. Results help locate problems; verify a blocked request before treating it as a missing file.

supportingLinks.label: Read the local workflow checks and limitations

items.title: Manual checks, not an automatic schedule
items.body: The plugin runs when you start a scan in the dashboard. Plan periodic checks after migrations or content changes. Large sites and image servers that block HEAD requests need extra care.

changelog.label: Status refresh
changelog.body: Plugin page copy and public metadata were refreshed to align with the current Kreativ WP maintenance positioning.

changelog.label: Release note link added
changelog.body: The plugin page now points to a dedicated update post so visitors can move from the plugin page into concrete release context.

quickStart: In WordPress, open Plugins → Add New Plugin and search for “Kreativ Broken Image Finder”, or upload the ZIP. Install and activate it on staging first.
Open the Kreativ Broken Image Finder menu and choose “Run Full Scan”. Keep the dashboard open while the batches complete.
Review the summary and filter the results by post type, source, or response code. The scanner checks content source URLs and featured images; CSS backgrounds are outside this scope.
Open each affected post, confirm the image really is unavailable, and repair or replace it. A blocked HEAD request can need manual verification. Run another scan after cleanup.
